reason: The text contains the named character Arnan (אָרְנָן הַיְבוּסִי), a Jebusite property owner, who is not a leader. While the primary named characters—David (king), Joab (military commander), and Gad (prophet/seer)—are indeed leaders, Arnan appears multiple times by name yet is portrayed as a common person of property who bows respectfully to King David and offers his threshing floor. He explicitly functions as a non-leader character in the narrative.
